messages:
deepak: heads-up — i'm seeing 18 GPU attach failures in us-east1-az1 after a brief network partition (~12s). nodes report local NVMe switching to readonly + IOPS collapse, causing kubelet attach timeouts.

miriam: same here, scheduler backlog spike, pods stuck Pending with AttachVolumeTimeout. These are dedicated pools, not preemptible.

chad: any dmesg / nvme logs? paste a snippet?

deepak: here's the tail from one host:
```
[ 12345.678901] nvme nvme0: reset controller
[ 12345.679012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 987654321
[ 12345.679123] Buffer I/O error on dev nvme0n1, logical block 123456
[ 12345.679234] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): error: ext4_journal_start_sb: Detected aborted journal
```

sre-robot: alert: local-nvme-iops-drop detected on cluster-us-east1. Affected hosts: 18. Severity: P2.

miriam: looks like firmware reset + IO error combo. Could be NVMe controller flapping after the partitioned network path (storage controller lost ACKs).

deepak: confirmed: kernel shows network reconnect at same timestamp as nvme reset.

chad: plan: 1) drain the 18 hosts (no new GPU attaches) 2) hold the cleaner/scrub job on those hosts 3) patch sysctl to reduce IO queue depth temporarily.

miriam: ack. stopping janitor on affected hosts now: `systemctl stop ephemeral-janitor` — will reroute scrub to warm hosts.

deepak: draining started, expected 45min to finish all GPU jobs. adding a soft-failover policy to route new attaches to us-west1.

deploy-bot: 6 new jobs rescheduled to us-west1 due to attach-failure policy.

chad: for mitigation can we try toggling nvme ctrl reset policy? `echo 1 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/device/reset` (manual) — but we should coordinate to avoid data loss.

deepak: prefer vendor ticket — mass manual resets increase risk. raising HW ticket with vendor + sending SMART logs.

miriam: also flagging cost impact: routing to us-west1 will increase egress + instance hours — estimate ~$1200 for the next 2 hours if we keep rescheduling.

deepak: noted. I'll update oncall and post an incident update. thanks all :thumbsup:

chad: follow-up: after draining we'll enable a conservative scrub window + drop cleaner parallelism from 16->4 on the cluster. should reduce contention.

deepak: will implement after hosts are safe. last check-in: any sign of corruption beyond IO errors?

miriam: no persistent ext4 corruptions observed yet, just journal abort warnings. continuing fsck on drained hosts as precaution.

sre-robot: incident-update: P2 -> monitoring. Next update in 15m.
